transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-14 16:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Recording ID ff-20270414-saffron-0092
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nandan (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (CISO, Saffron), Markus Ho (Head of Platform), Ravi Patel (Cloud Architect)
---
Summary: quick security intake focused on encryption/KMS strategy, SSO/SAML integration (Okta), RBAC model, audit log retention, and deployment preference (hosted vs dedicated vs private with HSM). Customer has strict PCI-adjacent controls and wants clarity on customer-managed keys and auditability.
Topics: SOC2 status, ISO roadmap, SSO/SAML, RBAC roles, audit logs & retention, encryption at rest with CMKs/HSM, private deployment options, redaction and telemetry.
---
[00:00] Jared: Alright everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jared from Redwood, with Priya our SE. Could everyone do a quick intro?
[00:08] Lena: Lena here, CISO at Saffron, been handling our compliance stuff. We're looking at LLMs for search + customer support summaries but need to lock down security first.
[00:16] Markus: Markus — platform lead, curious about deployment tradeoffs, latency and ops.
[00:20] Ravi: Ravi, cloud architect, I own our Azure infra and KMS/HSM stuff.
[00:24] Priya: Thanks — quick outline, we'll run through our security posture, focus on KMS and retention requirements and then Q&A.
[00:33] [00:33] Jared: Quick Q — are you leaning hosted, dedicated, or fully private?
[00:37] Lena: We prefer private/VPC or on-prem because of the PCI-adjacent data and our auditors; but open to dedicated if we can bring our own keys and get full audit logs.
[00:48] Priya: Totally — Redwood supports hosted with service-managed keys, dedicated reserved pools with options for BYOK, and private deployments with customer-managed network. For keys we do KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM-based flows for on-prem.
[00:59] [01:00] Ravi: When you say HSM-based flows, do you have an integration pattern for Azure Dedicated HSM or on-prem thales/equivalent?
[01:06] Priya: Yes, we've worked with Azure Key Vault with HSM-protected keys and customer managed keys (CMK). For on-prem HSM we can integrate via KMIP or an HSM gateway — depends on your topology. We'll put together a feasibility note.
[01:19] Markus: One of our constraints — audit logs need to be retained 7 years for certain flows, is that doable?
[01:25] Jared: Can you tell me which logs specifically? Platform-level audit logs, token-level request traces, or the application-level transcripts?
[01:33] Lena: Mainly access/audit logs for admin actions, user access to PII transcripts, and some redaction evidence. We need tamper-evident logs for our auditors.
[01:42] Priya: Our platform captures admin console events, model route invocations, token-level cost traces and full request/response logging if enabled. Default retention is 90 days in hosted, but extended retention is available as an add-on for dedicated/private — and for private you control retention via your storage. Tamper evidence can be achieved using append-only storage + periodic checksums; we've done integrations with SIEMs too.
[02:02] [02:02] Ravi: So for hosted with CMK — keys live in our Azure Key Vault, Redwood uses envelope encryption, but the key material never leaves our vault?
[02:11] Priya: Correct — envelope encryption where Redwood's service uses a data encryption key (DEK) wrapped by your CMK. We never persist your raw CMK. For some dedicated flows we can do a short-lived unwrap in a bounded environment, and logs show key usage.
[02:24] Jared: There's sometimes confusion — customers ask for HSM-backed signing of logs. We also support exporting signed log manifests; we'll include an example with the security pack.
[02:34] Markus: SSO — we use Okta, want SCIM provisioning and SAML 2.0 for auth. Do you support role mappings and just-in-time provisioning?
[02:43] Priya: Yes, SAML SSO is supported (Okta, Azure AD, Ping). SCIM provisioning is supported for user lifecycle. RBAC supports both role-mapped groups and attribute-based rules. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles.
[02:55] [02:55] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk)
[02:57] Lena: For RBAC we need separation: admin, security auditor (read-only access to logs), viewer, and service account roles. Can you restrict token access so service accounts cannot export raw transcripts?
[03:08] Priya: Yes, granular scopes — token-level policies can restrict read vs write, and we support sample-level redaction policies and field-level encryption for PII at rest. Service accounts can be limited to generate embeddings only, for example.
[03:22] Ravi: How about data in transit between Redwood and our VPC if we do a private deployment — do you support private peering or VPN tunnels?
[03:30] Jared: For Redwood Private we do customer-managed networking — options include VPC peering, private link-style endpoints, or an on-prem gateway. We'll need to see your topology diagram.
[03:41] Markus: Any SOC2/ISO statuses we should be aware of? Our procurement requires SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 ideally.
[03:49] Jared: Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified — we'll share the report excerpt. ISO 27001 is in progress and we can share the compliance roadmap. (note: link to security pack would be shared)
[03:59] [04:00] Lena: Do you support Customer Key Rotation policies enforced by our KMS? We need monthly rotation and documented rotation events.
[04:07] Priya: Rotation can be managed in your KMS; Redwood re-wraps DEKs accordingly. We log key usage events and rotation timestamps. We'll surface rotation events in the audit stream.
[04:18] Ravi: For private deployment with on-prem HSM, latency matters — if we keep unwrap calls local that's preferred. Is there an execution model where Redwood nodes run in our VPC and call local HSMs?
[04:29] Priya: Yes — private deployment nodes can be provisioned in your VPC so KMS/HSM calls stay within network. For dedicated hosted pools we can also support an HSM gateway deployed in your environment that the pool calls over private connectivity.
[04:41] [04:41] Markus: Are transcripts and artifacts stored encrypted at rest? Who has access to unredacted content?
[04:47] Priya: All persisted data is encrypted at rest. Access to unredacted content is restricted — by default only tenant service accounts and roles you grant have access. For hosted environments, Redwood SRE with emergency access have strict controls and all access is logged and audited. For private they don't have access unless you enable a support tunnel.
[05:03] Jared: Quick demo of RBAC mapping (Priya screenshares) — (screen noise, inaudible).
[05:16] [05:16] Priya: (explaining) here you map Okta group names to roles; you can create a compliance-only role that only reads logs and cannot view model outputs.
[05:27] Lena: That would help. For some regulators we need an immutable chain for audit evidence — do you support exporting signed manifests to our archive bucket?
[05:36] Priya: We can export logs to your S3/Azure blob and sign manifests; for private you can enforce immutability policies on the storage side. We'll include a sample export pipeline in the notes.
[05:47] [05:47] Ravi: What about masking/redaction? If the model output contains PII we want deterministic redaction and an audit trail showing redaction happened.
[05:56] Priya: We provide post-processing redaction hooks and can also stripe unique placeholders so the raw content is stored only in encrypted blobs accessible by authorized roles. Redaction events are logged with user and timestamp.
[06:08] Jared: Any legal requirements about data residency? You mentioned PCI-adjacent — do you have EU residency needs?
[06:14] Lena: Mostly US but for some customers we might need EU region processing. So regional routing is needed.
[06:20] Priya: We have region-aware routing and can pin workloads to regions or private deployment in EU regions.
[06:26] [06:26] Markus: Let's talk about what would block us from moving forward — for procurement the checklist is SOC2 + SLA, KMS BYOK, RBAC & SCIM, and 7-year log retention or an export path. Also need understanding of support & incident response SLAs.
[06:40] Jared: Good list. SLA and enterprise contract details we can send over; for incident response we have an on-call rotation and security contact process — we can share the runbook.
[06:50] Lena: One more — do you provide pen test evidence or allow us to run a pen test against the private deployment?
[06:56] Priya: Yes, for private and dedicated, customers can run penetration tests with coordinated windows; for hosted we have allowed penetration testing scopes. We'll include policy language.
[07:07] [07:07] (longer discussion about procurement windows, timeline)
[10:12] Jared: Let's be practical — for a pilot would you want a small dedicated pool or a private VPC deployment?
[10:20] Markus: Pilot as dedicated pool first with BYOK and extended logs — if that meets latency and retention we'll consider Private.
[10:27] Ravi: Agreed — also need a benchmark of 99th percentile latency for our 2k token prompts.
[10:33] Priya: We'll run a benchmark and share token-level latency percentiles, plus cost estimates for batching and caching recommendations.
[10:41] [10:41] (notes about pricing and Reserved capacity)
[12:00] Lena: On the legal side — we need to know how subprocessor lists are handled and whether Redwood uses third-party inference accelerators in hosted mode.
[12:10] Jared: We provide a subprocessor list and can provide an addendum if needed. Hosted does sometimes use cloud GPU providers — for dedicated/private we can isolate on reserved hardware.
[12:23] Markus: For e-discovery we might need ability to pull transcripts on demand with audit trail. Is that supported?
[12:30] Priya: Yes, you can export transcripts with associated audit metadata. We can create an e-discovery export job that includes hash manifests.
[12:38] [12:38] Ravi: A few low-level questions — are KV caches persisted and how are they encrypted? If we want to flush caches on demand how is that controlled?
[12:47] Priya: KV caches are ephemeral by default but we have configurable cache persistence for performance. If persisted they are encrypted at rest and can be flushed via API or by role-based console control; we log flush events.
[12:58] Jared: Also note we have quality-of-service routing and fallbacks which we'll document so you know how failover behaves.
[13:06] Lena: For auditors we need demonstration of access revoke. Can you demo revoking a user's SAML session and show logs?
[13:13] Priya: We can replay a revoke flow in a follow-up demo; the log will show revoke event and any active tokens terminated.
[13:21] [13:21] (some on-call scheduling chat)
[14:00] Markus: Anything else? I want to ensure our security folks see the sample manifest and the HSM integration pattern.
[14:06] Priya: We'll attach a sample architecture diagram and a KMIP example.
[14:10] Jared: I'll also include a redwood security pack link with SOC2 excerpt, pen test summary, and data handling docs (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack/saffron).
[14:20] Lena: Sounds good. If you could confirm the retention add-on pricing that helps procurement.
[14:26] Jared: Will include pricing tiers for 90-day default, 1 year, 3 year, and archive export options for multi-year retention.
[14:33] [14:33] (closing)
[14:35] Priya: Quick recap: we'll send SOC2 docs, HSM/KMS feasibility note, sample log export pipeline, retention pricing, and schedule pilot benchmark week of 4/26.
[14:46] Jared: Next steps noted — thanks all.
[14:50] Lena: Thanks, bye.
